Priestly Garments
PREEST-lee GAR-muhnts
noun
From priestly + garments; the holy vestments of the Aaronic priesthood, made for glory and for beauty.

Biblical Definition

The priestly garments were the holy vestments which the LORD commanded for Aaron and his sons, made for glory and for beauty, that they might minister in the priest’s office. The high priest wore the ephod of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen; the breastplate of judgment set with twelve precious stones bearing the names of the twelve tribes, that Aaron might bear their names upon his heart before the LORD continually; the robe of the ephod with bells and pomegranates; the mitre with a plate of pure gold engraved Holiness to the LORD; the broidered coat, the girdle, and the linen breeches. Every part was significant: the names of the tribes borne on the shoulders and the heart spoke of the priest representing the people before God; the bells that his sound be heard when he went in; the golden plate that he bear the iniquity of the holy things. All the garments were given by revelation and made by men filled with the Spirit of wisdom. They foreshadowed the great High Priest, the Lord Jesus, who bears His people’s names upon His heart, who is clothed in the true holiness the plate proclaimed, and who needs no garments to cover sin, having none. The dictionary honors the priestly garments as a divinely-appointed picture of the mediatorial office, fulfilled in Christ, who represents His people before the Father, bears their names upon His heart, and is Himself the Holiness to the LORD that the golden plate foreshadowed.

Webster 1828 Definition

The holy vestments of the Aaronic priesthood, made for glory and beauty; figures of the priest bearing the people before God, fulfilled in Christ the great High Priest.

PRIESTLY GARMENTS, the holy vestments of Aaron, for glory and beauty.

The ephod, the breastplate of judgment with twelve stones, the robe.

The mitre bore a golden plate: Holiness to the LORD.

Aaron bore the tribes’ names on his shoulders and his heart.

Figures of Christ, who bears His people’s names before the Father.

Key Scripture

Exo 28:2 — "And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother for glory and for beauty."

Exo 28:29 — "And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart, when he goeth in unto the holy place, for a memorial before the LORD continually."

Exo 28:36 — "And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD."

Heb 4:14 — "Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession."

Modern Corruption

The garments are claimed to justify ornate clerical vestments, or dismissed as mere ancient costume; they foreshadow Christ’s mediatorial office, now fulfilled.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Two errors attend the priestly garments. The first appeals to them to justify ornate sacerdotal vestments and a sacrificing priesthood in the Christian church—as though the shadow were to be perpetuated. But the Aaronic garments belonged to a priesthood that has passed: Christ is the one High Priest, and the New Testament knows no order of vestmented sacrificing priests, but a priesthood of all believers. The second error dismisses the garments as mere ancient costume, missing their rich significance.

The principle to recover is that the priestly garments foreshadowed the mediatorial office of Christ. Made for glory and for beauty (Exo 28:2), every part preached the gospel: Aaron bore the names of the tribes upon his heart for a memorial before the LORD continually (Exo 28:29), as Christ bears His people upon His heart in heaven; the golden plate, Holiness to the LORD (Exo 28:36), proclaimed the holiness in which the priest must come, which Christ alone possesses perfectly. We have a great High Priest passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God (Heb 4:14); the garments are fulfilled in Him, and the believer needs no earthly priest, having the true and abiding one.
